bib.title: DROP: A Reading Comprehension Benchmark Requiring Discrete Reasoning Over Paragraphs

question: Can reading comprehension systems perform discrete reasoning (counting, addition, sorting) over paragraphs, which existing datasets like SQuAD do not require?
hypothesis: Questions needing discrete reasoning over paragraph content, collected adversarially against a baseline, will be far harder for current systems than prior datasets.
contributions: DROP, a crowdsourced, adversarially-created 96k-question English reading comprehension benchmark requiring discrete reasoning
Evaluation of heuristic, semantic parsing and SQuAD-style RC baselines
NAQANet, a QANet extension with limited numerical reasoning reaching 47.0% F1

method.summary: Passages were extracted from Wikipedia (NFL summaries, history), and Mechanical Turk workers wrote questions that a live BiDAF model could not answer. Dev and test answers were validated with extra annotations. Heuristic, semantic parsing and RC baselines plus a numerically-aware QANet (NAQANet) were evaluated with EM and a numeracy-focused F1.
method.task: reading comprehension requiring discrete reasoning over a paragraph (answers are spans, numbers or dates)

datasets.name: DROP
datasets.split: random by passage: train 80% (5565 passages, 77,409 questions), dev 10% (582, 9,536), test 10% (588, 9,622)
datasets.source: Wikipedia (Oct 2018 dump plus scraping), crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk; 60k USD budget; 5 USD per HIT, about 10 USD/hour
datasets.preprocessing: 0.7% of questions marked invalid in validation and filtered out; at least two extra answers collected for each dev/test question; for span-only RC models 45% of train questions not answerable by a span were omitted

datasets.name: SQuAD 1.1
datasets.preprocessing: used only to report baseline EM (BiDAF 66.8, QANet 72.7, QANet+ELMo 78.7, BERT 84.7)

datasets.name: WikiTableQuestions
datasets.preprocessing: question style inspiration and KDG parser design; not trained on

models.name: NAQANet
models.architecture: QANet with four output heads (passage span, question span, count 0-9, signed-number arithmetic expression) plus answer-type classifier

other.arithmetic_search: only addition/subtraction of two numbers searched

models.name: BERT
models.init_from: pretrained BERT large uncased (Hugging Face pytorch-pretrained-bert)

other.drop_to_squad: first match used as gold span

models.name: KDG semantic parser (Syn Dep, OpenIE, SRL)
models.architecture: grammar-constrained parser over table built from paragraph

training.objective: marginal likelihood over all answer-matching executions (spans, counts, sign assignments); KDG maximises marginal likelihood of logical forms found by exhaustive search to preset depth
training.hardware: GPU (memory-limited); computations on beaker.org with Google Cloud credits

other.note: NAQANet hyperparameters stated to equal QANet baseline but not listed

inference.decoding: KDG: beam search for most likely logical form then execute; NAQANet: answer type chosen greedily, then best answer within type
inference.samples: not stated; single reported number per system

metrics.name: Exact Match (EM)
metrics.definition: SQuAD implementation: removes articles and simple normalisation; max over gold answers

metrics.name: Numeracy-focused F1
metrics.definition: macro-averaged bag-of-words overlap F1 (SQuAD-based); 0 if number mismatch between gold and prediction; multi-span answers aligned greedily one-to-one then averaged; max over gold answers

baselines: Syn Dep / OpenIE / SRL semantic parsers (KDG)
eval.protocol: Dev and hidden test. Human performance estimated by the authors collectively answering 560 test questions. No seeds or significance tests stated.

evidence.quote: our settings differ from the original paper only in the batch size (16 v.s. 32)

results.setup: DROP test, BERT large uncased baseline vs human on 560 test questions
results.quote: the best systems only achieve 32.7% F1 on our generalized accuracy metric, while expert human performance is 96.4%

results.claim: NAQANet complete model reaches 47.0% F1 on test.

results.claim: NAQANet gains 14.3 points F1 over the best baseline.
results.quote: This model reaches 47% F1, a 14.3% absolute increase over the best baseline system.

results.claim: Subtraction is the most common reasoning type (28.8%); comparison 18.2%, selection 19.4%.
Semantic-parser search yields logical forms for only 34% of train data (SRL/Syn Dep), 25% with OpenIE; only 13% of 60 sampled questions had non-spurious logical forms.
results.quote: the search was able to yield logical forms for 34% of the training data, whereas with OpenIE, it was only 25%

results.claim: Error analysis of 100 NAQANet errors: arithmetic 51%, counting 30%, domain knowledge 23%, coreference 6%, combinations 40%.
results.quote: arithmetic operations (evident in 51% of the errors), counting (30%)

results.claim: Total Mechanical Turk budget was 60k USD.
results.quote: a total Mechanical Turk budget of 60k USD

limits: Weak supervision: only answer strings, no reasoning type, so spurious logical forms hurt training.
NAQANet handles only counts 0-9 and addition/subtraction of up to two numbers.
Human performance estimated by the authors themselves on 560 test questions.
Heavy skew to NFL game summaries and history passages; some questions need sports domain knowledge.
Adversary was BiDAF, no longer state of the art; only systems of 2019 evaluated.
No seeds, optimizer or learning rate given for baselines; hyperparameters deferred to the code release.
Numeric answers restricted to questions stating a unit, to ease evaluation.

terms.definition: Discrete Reasoning Over the content of Paragraphs
F1 is 0 when there is a number mismatch between gold and predicted answers regardless of other word overlap
